about: Lesson F8 (f08-large-loads), 2026-11-05. A data center appears only as a load: its size, its shape over the day and the year, the wait for its grid connection, and what it brings to a town. Prairie Town and its data-center campus are fictional; the campus's size, draw, building time, wait, jobs, tax and cooling are illustrative. The town's hourly demand follows real Southwest Power Pool shapes (town_days.json, town_year.json; EIA-930, 2025) scaled so its highest hour of 2025 is town.peakMW, as lessons 0 and 2 do. Real-world numbers carry their primary source, URL and date. The real-world box quotes approved excerpt sentences E7.4 and E7.5 (excerpt:code), word for word; no other sentence describes that study.

coolingSource.note: Supports: a condenser water loop carries heat to a cooling tower, where evaporation removes it; tower water use comes mainly from evaporation and is high for constant loads such as data centers; air-cooled heat rejection is an alternative. The electricity remark on dry cooling is qualitative.
